$comment: AUTHORED SOURCE — not generated. scripts/build-tokens.mts reads this file and emits app/tokens.generated.css and lib/generated/tokens.ts. The `linear()` stop lists were sampled from the spring parameters recorded beside them; if you change a spring you must resample, and the sampler is documented in `sampling` below.

cssNaming.$comment: A spring token emits ONE custom property holding a `linear()` easing, plus a matching `--opsin-duration-{name}` holding the settle time. They are always used together: a spring easing paired with an unrelated duration is not the spring any more.

rules: Motion never carries urgency. An urgent reading is urgent because of its word, its icon and its position, never because it moved faster or pulsed. A pulsing red card is the single most common alarm-fatigue defect in consumer health UI and it is banned outright.
Morph, do not swap. When a value changes, animate the value in place; do not cross-fade one card out and another in. A swap reads as 'a different reading'; a morph reads as 'this reading changed'.

Reduced motion is per token, not a kill switch. Every token below declares its own `reducedMotion` fallback. Removing all motion removes the cue that something changed, which is worse for a reader who is tracking a number over time.
Nothing that conveys a health value may animate for longer than `duration-deliberate`. A reader waiting to see a number is not being delighted.

sampling.model: Damped harmonic oscillator, unit displacement, zero initial velocity. x(t) = 1 - e^(-zeta*w0*t) * (cos(wd*t) + (zeta*w0/wd) * sin(wd*t)) for zeta < 1, with w0 = sqrt(k/m), zeta = c / (2*sqrt(k*m)), wd = w0*sqrt(1 - zeta^2); the critically damped and overdamped closed forms are used when zeta >= 1.
sampling.settleRule: The duration is the last time at which |x(t) - 1| exceeds the settle threshold, rounded up to the millisecond. This is why the durations are odd numbers: they are measured, not chosen.
sampling.$comment: 21 evenly spaced samples across the settle time. Fewer than about 16 makes the overshoot visibly polygonal; more than about 24 buys nothing a viewer can see and bloats every stylesheet that inlines the token.

spring-snap.use: Direct manipulation only: a switch the reader just flipped, a segmented control, a pressed button settling. The only token in the system that overshoots, and it overshoots by 1.5% — enough to feel physical, not enough to look playful.
spring-snap.doNotUse: Anything that displays a health value. A number that overshoots its target has, for one frame, displayed a number that is not true.

reducedMotion.note: Snap to the end state. The reader initiated it, so there is nothing to explain.

spring-settle.use: The workhorse for chrome: popovers, tooltips, menus, chips appearing and disappearing.
spring-settle.doNotUse: Full-screen transitions, where 382ms reads as hesitant.

reducedMotion.note: A short cross-fade. Keeps the 'something appeared' cue without the travel.

spring-calm.use: Health values. A range bar filling, a dial sweeping to its reading, a sparkline drawing, a number counting to its value. Slightly overdamped (zeta just over 1) so it never overshoots and never bounces.
spring-calm.doNotUse: Anything the reader is waiting on to make a decision inside a form.

reducedMotion.note: Render the final value immediately. Never animate a health value for a reader who has asked for less motion.

spring-sheet.use: Large surfaces travelling a long distance: sheets, dialogs, full-screen pushes. Overdamped, because a sheet that bounces at the top of its travel reads as a dropped object.
spring-sheet.doNotUse: Small elements. At this duration a 4px move looks broken.

reducedMotion.note: Cross-fade in place. A sheet that appears with no travel still needs to be seen to appear.

ease-standard.use: Non-spring transitions where a spring would be overkill: colour, opacity, border. Fast out, slow in.

ease-enter.use: Something arriving from off-screen or from nothing. Decelerating, because an arrival should feel like it is coming to rest.

ease-exit.use: Something leaving. Accelerating and shorter than its enter, because a reader does not need to watch a dismissal finish.

duration-instant.use: State change with no travel: hover tint, focus ring, checkbox tick.

duration-fast.use: Small elements moving a small distance.

duration-base.use: The default for chrome that is not spring-driven.

duration-slow.use: Layout change: a list reflowing, a card expanding.

duration-deliberate.use: The ceiling. Used for a first-run reveal or a consent sheet, where the point is that the reader notices. Nothing may exceed it.

reducedMotion.policy: Every token above declares its own fallback and build-tokens.mts emits them inside the query. What survives: opacity changes under 120ms, and any change of state that would otherwise be invisible. What does not: travel, scale, rotation, parallax, and every animation of a health value.
reducedMotion.$comment: The reason this is per token rather than a global `animation: none` is that a reader who asks for reduced motion still needs to know that a value changed. Removing the cue entirely trades a vestibular problem for a comprehension problem.
